title: Intent-based undo
evidenceStatus: One original authored request, five judgments; frozen component equals current Undo block; 32 offline subset and restoration checks plus reproduced state defects
summary: The saved run correctly selects the two color changes, but changing a selection or completing a rerun reverses an already applied undo. Old suggestions also apply after request edits and replace manual review. A real command history with separate proposals, actor identity and conflict checks is needed before claiming preservation of unrelated work.
strengths: Jev chooses an edit subset while code owns all replacement values and rendering.
The visitor can inspect and adjust selections before explicitly applying them.
All 32 subsets and 32 restoration checks pass on the fixed five-unique-field fixture.
Original recorded answers and source were checked against frozen commit 4c0c40d; no provider calls were needed.

findings.title: Proposal edits reverse an applied undo
findings.evidence: src/new-experiments.tsx:641 rebuilds the document from fixed after values; lines 707 and 759 set applied false after selection edits and completed requests. Actual callbacks restore blue/sage immediately after accepting terracotta/cream.
findings.impact: Accepted changes are not durable transactions, so successive undo requests cannot compose.
findings.fix: Separate committed document and transaction history from draft proposals; selection and inference must not mutate committed work.

findings.title: Obsolete decisions apply to a new request and overwrite manual selection
findings.evidence: src/new-experiments.tsx:734 changes only query, and line 753 accepts every response. The probe changes to title-only, selects e4, receives an old color response and ends with e1/e3 under the title-only request.
findings.impact: The next apply and exported state associate the wrong semantic decision with the visitor's intent.
findings.fix: Bind proposals to document, history, request and selection revisions; invalidate old suggestions and retain late responses only for inspection.

findings.title: The fixed projection cannot establish preservation of user edits
findings.evidence: src/new-experiments.tsx:596 has five unique-field assignments without actors or dependencies; line 669 calls a preview editable despite zero design-edit controls. Synthetic red-to-blue agent and blue-to-green user events return red when undoing the earlier event and blue when undoing both.
findings.impact: The fixture excludes repeated writes, manual work and structural dependencies, which are the central selective-undo cases. Synthetic extension failures are not currently reachable UI actions.
findings.fix: Use stable-ID commands with actors, transaction groups, preconditions and a declared retained-event/dependency policy; provide real design-edit controls.

findings.title: One literal request does not measure semantic value or final outcomes
findings.evidence: scripts/record.ts:71 records one five-edit request, matched exactly by an accent/background field rule. The save helper at line 18 retains no request/history snapshot or independent outcomes; recorded and live instruction text differs.
findings.impact: Five sensible scores cannot establish general accuracy, calibrated confidence, preserved work or reduced review effort.
findings.fix: Retain immutable inputs and prompt versions, independently label varied histories and expected final documents, and compare deterministic filters and manual selection under matched controls.

simulation.title: An editor with durable selective undo
simulation.description: Let the visitor edit an apartment page alongside logged agent changes, request an actor- and meaning-specific reversal, inspect a separate preview, resolve conflicts, apply one transaction, then continue editing and undo or redo without losing newer work.
simulation.jevsRole: Classify visible candidate operations as undo, keep or needs review using the request and versioned history; never invent replacement document values.
simulation.codeRole: Store stable-ID commands, actors, revisions and dependencies; compute exact previews, preserve retained later assignments, detect structural conflicts, commit atomically and manage compensating transactions and redo branches.
acceptanceCriteria: Request edits, selection edits and model responses leave the committed document unchanged.
Each accepted transaction applies once and matches an independently specified final snapshot.
Later retained assignments survive removal of earlier assignments; removing all assignments restores the base value.
Late results cannot replace manual selections or write across history revisions.
Structural dependencies produce an explicit safe result or a visible unresolved conflict.
Undo/redo respect preconditions and never discard a newer branch silently.
Export preserves history, request, raw decisions, manual adjustments, conflicts, transaction and final document hash.

evaluation.design: Independently annotate 48 development and 240 held-out twelve-operation histories across six equal strata. Two paraphrases and two seeded presentations per history compare current score/0.5 and proposed undo/keep/review protocols: 1920 logical requests and 23040 edit decisions before retries. Use independent expected snapshots and adjudicated ambiguity outcomes, paired 10000-resample bootstrap clustered by history, 1000 offline action schedules, and 12 reviewers completing 12 counterbalanced tasks each with frozen decisions.
baselines: Deterministic field, actor and temporal filters
Manual history selection with the same preview
Oracle selection through the same transaction engine
Plain last-action undo, explicitly limited to chronological reversal
metrics: Exact intended subset and exact final-state success
Stale writes, duplicate commits and loss of retained edits
Provider availability, retries, latency and cost
Reviewed-operation count, correction effort and completion time
Clustered 95% intervals; provisional lower bound at least 90% exact outcome success with no observed unrelated writes

coverage.current: One request, one five-edit history and five scores. Thirty-two subset checks assess deterministic behavior only; no external benchmark or productivity study.
coverage.full: 48 development plus 240 held-out histories, six strata of 40 test histories and twelve operations each. Held-out protocols total 1920 requests/23040 decisions; 24-history pilot is a 192-request subset. Offline 1000-schedule tests and 144 reviewer sessions require no extra model calls.
coverage.feasibility: Feasible without external datasets or weights. Needs a real transaction engine, two independent annotators plus adjudication, payload checks under 100 KB/128 questions, and a future evaluation budget. No planned model calls or participant study were performed during this audit.

libraries.name: Immer patches
libraries.use: Capture forward/inverse document patches and apply checked transactions. Stable IDs, preconditions and selective-undo conflict policy remain application responsibilities.

libraries.name: fast-check command testing
libraries.use: Generate, shrink and replay edit/response/apply/undo schedules against independent revision and protected-edit invariants.
